welcome.title: Welcome to Sound Master’s Lair
welcome.body: Build living soundscapes for your sessions. This quick tour walks through tracks, loop windows, groups, stages, and sharing. Start by adding your first track.
welcome.alt: Empty Tracks page with a "Create your first track" card

addTrack.title: Add a track
addTrack.body: Start by creating your first track. Give the track a name and paste a YouTube link. That’s all it takes to bring audio into your library.
addTrack.alt: Add Track dialog with a name field and a YouTube link field

manageTracks.title: Manage your tracks
manageTracks.body: Each track has a row menu. From there, you can edit its details, edit its loop windows, open the source, or delete it.
manageTracks.alt: Tracks list with an open row menu showing Edit track, Edit windows, Open source, Delete

windows.title: Loop windows
windows.body: Do you want to play only a part or some parts of a track? A window is a slice of a track that may be looped seamlessly. Set the from/to range, a crossfade for a clean seam, and preview before saving.
windows.alt: Windows editor showing a loop range, crossfade strength, and a preview player

groups.title: Groups
groups.body: Groups let you organise tracks by mood or scene - combat, ambient, tavern. Start by creating your first group.
groups.alt: Empty Groups page with a "Create your first group" card

groupName.title: Name the group
groupName.body: Give the group a nice, recognisable name.
groupName.alt: Create Group dialog with a name field

groupTracks.title: Add tracks to a group
groupTracks.body: Search and select the tracks that belong in this group. A track can live in more than one group.
groupTracks.alt: Edit tracks dialog with a searchable, selectable list of tracks

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.body: A session holds the stages for one game - think of it as your setup, where you control the flow of music. You can of course have multiple sessions for different setups. Create your first session to get started.
sessions.alt: Stages page with a "Create your first session" card

stages.title: Stages
stages.body: Stages are the application's bread and butter - your play surface. Each one plays a track or a playlist independently on demand during the session. Start by creating your first stage.
stages.alt: Session with a "Create your first stage" card

createStage.title: Create a stage
createStage.body: Name the stage and optionally pick the track which should be initially selected.
createStage.alt: Create Stage dialog with a name field and a track selector

playStage.title: Play a stage
playStage.body: Hit play to start playback for that stage. Choose a group, track, and window - even mid-play. Additionally, switch to playlist mode if you need to play through all tracks in a selected group.
playStage.alt: Stage player with group/track/window selectors, single/playlist toggle, and a seek bar

settings.title: Playback settings
settings.body:
Per-stage options:
  • Loop mode - controls how track windows repeat: Off plays once, Loop repeats seamlessly, and Sequence cycles through all available windows in order.
  • Overplay - lets this stage play in parallel with others. Starting another stage won’t mute this one.
  • Keyboard shortcut - toggle the stage without clicking.
settings.alt: Playback settings popover with loop mode, overplay, and keyboard shortcut options

workshop.title: Sharing
workshop.body: Have a track with nice windows, tight crossfades and want to share it? Publish your tracks so other Sound Masters can find and subscribe to them - and discover theirs.
workshop.alt: Sharing "My tracks" dialog listing tracks with publish status and subscribers

profile.title: Your profile
profile.body: See your current limits, change your password, email, name, set your preffered language, and re-open this tutorial any time from the “?” button here.
profile.alt: User profile page showing account details and rank & limits

faq.title: Questions & answers
faq.body: A few things that come up often:
faq.q1: What happens when I switch the track / window mid-play?
faq.a1: The current track stops while the stage crossfades into the newly selected one.
faq.q2: Will a stopped stage start playing when I pre-select a track?
faq.a2: No. A stage won't play until you hit start. You can even select a different group to prepare a new track selection while the stage is still playing, without changing the actual playback.
faq.q3: What happens if I hit play on a stage while another stage is playing?
faq.a3: By default the other stage stops while playback crossfades into the new one, so only one stage plays at a time. Enable Overplay in a stage’s playback settings to let it play in parallel with others instead.
faq.q4: Can other users edit the tracks I publish?
faq.a4: No. Other Sound Masters can subscribe to and play your published tracks. Only you can edit the original.
faq.q5: My track or window ends too abruptly and looping doesn't sound nice
faq.a5: Go to Tracks, select the Edit windows option for the specific track and update the crossfade length for the window or the whole track.
faq.q6: Sequence loop mode is not selectable on some tracks
faq.a6: Sequence mode needs at least two windows on a track to apply.
faq.q7: Background looping does not respect crossfades
faq.a7: Some browsers, for example Safari, simply do not allow processing multiple audio streams at once. In that case, try a different browser. The application was successfully tested on: Chrome, Edge, Brave and Firefox
faq.q8: Background looping does not work at all
faq.a8: This is mainly a problem with the YouTube IFrame API on mobile devices. The IFrame API does not provide a raw audio element that the underlying OS can process. But don't worry, there are workarounds. Try to minimise the browser window so it stays in focus, or turn on desktop mode.
